name: CascAid
description: Practise fictional psychiatric interviews with local language models, optional speech recognition, spoken replies, an experimental 3D character, and formative feedback.
compatibility: Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-Embedding run through local llama.cpp servers.
Optional speech input uses whisper.cpp; character speech uses HeadTTS and Kokoro-82M.
limitations: Early-stage educational research proof of concept for CASC-style psychiatric interviews. Cases and automated feedback are not clinically validated; feedback is not an examination mark or clinical decision support.

The documented model setup requires an Apple Silicon Mac; the reported evaluation host is an Apple M4 with 16 GiB unified memory. Other platforms and smaller memory configurations are not established by these sources.

Requires Node.js 22 or newer, npm and uv. Initial setup downloads models and runtimes; generation, recognition and synthesis then run locally without a hosted fallback. Enable the local backends explicitly; the default model backend returns scripted stand-in replies.
Speech input requires browser microphone permission. Audio is not saved by default, but transcripts are logged locally; a separate consent-based evaluation recorder can retain audio when enabled.

The optional 3D avatar is experimental and installation requires Blender 4.5.14. The optional fine-tuned student interpreter weights are not distributed; the documented Qwen fallback remains available.
Code is AGPL-3.0-only; cases, data and documentation are CC-BY-4.0. Downloaded models, voices, runtimes and avatar assets have separate licenses.
